title: Ihpetonga
summary: Ihpetonga is recorded by William Wallace Tooker as a name bestowed on Brooklyn Heights by Henry R. Schoolcraft. It is presented here as a descriptive name for the heights or high sandy banks of the Brooklyn bluff.
map_geometry_source: Approximate general marker for Brooklyn Heights bluff landscape described in Tooker entry 110; not an exact historic boundary or deed point.
history_content: The source cites Schoolcraft through Gowans for the statement that the heights of Brooklyn were described by Ihpetonga. It then critiques the linguistic derivation, preferring comparison with Mohegan, Massachusetts, and Delaware forms for heights or high sandy banks. The history is a descriptive language note rather than a boundary-specific land record.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Ihpetonga and Sphetonga. Sphetonga is treated as a cross-reference to Ihpetonga, a name applied to Brooklyn Heights for its high sandy banks.

Why Place Names Matter

“The names of places reflect a rich cultural heritage and tradition, diverse economic activities, and an identity that is rooted in the local environment, anchored in indigenous culture.”

— Rusli, Place Names: Preserving Cultural Heritage, Reflecting National Identity (2013), Introduction, first paragraph
land_loss_content: Ihpetonga shows how Indigenous-language terms and later scholarly naming were used to describe the landform of Brooklyn Heights. Recording Tooker's caution helps distinguish a descriptive linguistic entry from a documented deed name.
whereintheworld_content: The map placement is an approximate general point in Brooklyn Heights, near the bluff landscape overlooking the East River, not a boundary for the historic neighborhood or a claim of an exact named site.
